Float a ball on the surface so it keeps a hole open as it moves, or stand a pan of hot water on the ice until it melts through, and keep a hole open all winter so the gases can get out. samples.user: Which of the following is a type of pasta: lasagna, sushi, or burrito?
samples.pybot: Pasta comes down to six families, and the family decides the job: long strands (spaghetti, linguine and tagliatelle) for a ragu, a carbonara or a butter sauce the strands can carry; tubes (penne and rigatoni) for a baked dish, and a thick sauce that fills the tube; twists and shells (fusilli, farfalle and conchiglie) for a sauce with bits in it that needs something to cling to, and pasta salad; tiny shapes (orzo and stelline) for soup, and a salad that should not be all bulk; sheets (lasagne) for a bake, layered instead of tossed and filled (ravioli and tortellini) for a meal on its own with butter or a light sauce. The time goes by the shape as well: 8 to 9 minutes for thin strands, 10 to 11 for spaghetti and penne, 11 to 13 for rigatoni and tagliatelle, and 3 to 4 for the filled ones. Fresh pasta is 2 to 3 minutes, not the packet time.
samples.net: Long pasta - spaghetti, linguine, tagliatelle - is for thin sauces that coat it. Short shapes - penne, fusilli, rigatoni - hold chunkier sauces, and the ridges and tubes are there to catch them. Filled pasta - ravioli, tortellini - is a meal with its sauce inside. Dried is durum wheat and water; fresh is egg and soft wheat, cooks in two or three minutes, and is richer. Wholewheat is the same shapes with the bran left in, and takes a minute longer.
